newsitem.title: POLAND: Secondary Polish T-bill trade falls in Dec-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Secondary Polish T-bill trade falls in Dec-Feb.

text.p: Secondary turnover in Polish T-bills fell to 34 billion zlotys in December after peaking at 51.8 billion in November and stabilised at around 39 billion zlotys in January and February, the National Bank of Poland said.
It said February's secondary trade in T-bills totalled 38.84 billion zlotys, down from January's 39.87 billion.
The NBP said secondary trade in its bills slumped to 2.29 billion in February from 4.76 billion in January, 3.67 billion in December. In November the turnover peaked at 16.99 billion zlotys.
November was the last month when secondary T-bill turnover was taken into account in awarding banks primary T-bill market dealer status.
Average T-bill holdings in domestic non-financial client portfolios amounted to 8.14 billion zlotys in February, up from January's 7.55 billion and 8.02 billion in December.
